title: Bangladesh PM Rahman Blames India in Veiled Dig as Hasina Supporters' Unrest Spreads
excerpt: Tarique Rahman said the leaders who fled across the border serve "masters" there, as an Awami League lockdown brought arson attacks, arrests and the torching of Muhammad Yunus's ancestral home.
body:
• Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, without naming India, said the Awami League leaders who fled across the border serve “masters” there and are “conspiring against Bangladesh” — a veiled dig at New Delhi as violence spread on Thursday.
  • The unrest followed the government’s rejection of Sheikh Hasina’s request for a new passport to return from exile in India in December; her banned Awami League called a nationwide lockdown to end a week of protests.
  • Police said two ruling-party members were killed on Wednesday night, at least six buses and vans were torched, and 107 people were arrested in Dhaka in 24 hours; the ancestral home of former interim leader Muhammad Yunus was set on fire in Chattogram.
  • India’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and Awami League leaders, most in hiding, could not be reached, Reuters reported.

Fresh violence broke out in Bangladesh on Thursday as supporters of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina tried to bring businesses and public transport to a halt, and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman blamed India for the unrest without naming it. At a public event in the northern district of Lalmonirhat, Rahman said Awami League leaders “have not looked at the interests of Bangladesh and its people,” Reuters reported. “At the same time, the country across the border, where they have fled to, is their master … To satisfy those masters, they have again started conspiring against Bangladesh, and its people,” he said.

“Enough is enough. We must give a clear answer to these terrorists, arsonists and killers.”

— Tarique Rahman, Prime Minister of Bangladesh, at Lalmonirhat

A lockdown, arson attacks and a house set ablaze

The Awami League called Thursday’s nationwide lockdown at the end of a week-long campaign of protests and rallies against the government’s rejection of Hasina’s request for a new passport that would allow her to return. Hasina fled after a student uprising against her rule in August 2024, lives in exile in India, and has said she plans to return in December. The attempted shutdown was successful mostly in the southern districts where the League is strongest, Reuters reported.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Sa8j3rabI70

Police said two members of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party were killed on Wednesday night, while the houses of two BNP lawmakers in Hasina’s home district of Gopalganj were vandalised and set alight. At least six buses and pickup vans were set on fire along with a section of railway line, crude bomb blasts were reported across six districts overnight, and a bus and a truck were set on fire on Thursday on the Dhaka–Chattogram highway, with the bus passengers escaping unharmed. In a separate count, ANI reported at least four people killed in separate incidents over the past three days — one in Faridpur, one in Pirojpur and two in Narail. Unrelated protests by garment workers demanding higher wages also continued in some districts, with hundreds of workers blocking a highway into Dhaka and forcing factories to close.

Yunus’s ancestral home in the port city of Chattogram, about 300 km southeast of Dhaka, was set on fire late on Wednesday. Police officer Mozammel Haque said it was likely flammable substances had been thrown into an unused ground-floor room, and that Yunus’s paternal family members, who live on the upper floors, were safe. In Dhaka, police arrested 107 people suspected of links to the Awami League and its affiliated organisations in 24 hours, including former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid.

What each side says

Rahman’s government has accused Awami League leaders outside Bangladesh of fanning the violence and vowed action, according to Reuters; ANI’s account of the same rally quoted him saying people do not want politics involving arson, enforced disappearances and killings any more. Awami League leaders, most of them in hiding, could not be reached for comment, and India’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment, Reuters reported. To deter violence, 97 platoons of the paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh have fanned out across seven districts, including Gopalganj and Faridpur, a Guard spokesperson said; a BGB statement carried by ANI listed 96 platoons across Dhaka, Chattogram, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Gopalganj, Mymensingh and Faridpur, with five more platoons on standby.

Why it matters beyond Dhaka

The rising unrest in the nation of 175 million people — the world’s second-biggest garment exporter after China — threatens the fragile stability established since elections this year brought Rahman, a political opponent of Hasina’s outlawed Awami League, to power. After Hasina was ousted, relations with India deteriorated sharply under the interim government of Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus in Dhaka. Ties have improved slightly since Rahman took office in February, although tensions over Hasina’s continued presence in India remain a major irritant — and her stated plan to return in December now sits at the centre of the confrontation.
